discovery: Prediction and discovery of flat bands, correlated insulators and superconductivity in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene

nominees.name: Allan H. MacDonald
nominees.affiliation: University of Texas at Austin, USA

nominees.name: Rafi Bistritzer
nominees.affiliation: formerly University of Texas at Austin (now industry, Israel)

subfield: Condensed matter physics: two-dimensional quantum materials and strongly correlated electrons
motivation: Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted in 2011 that twisting two graphene sheets to a 'magic angle' near 1.1 degrees would collapse the Dirac bands into nearly flat moire minibands, where interactions would dominate. In 2018 Jarillo-Herrero's group realized this, finding correlated insulating states and unconventional superconductivity whose phase diagram echoes that of the cuprates. The twist angle turned out to be a new, continuously tunable control knob for quantum matter. This work created the field of moire and twistronic materials. Laboratories worldwide, including mine, now use these platforms to study correlated insulators, orbital magnetism, the fractional quantum anomalous Hall effect, and new plasmonic and polaritonic collective modes. Few recent discoveries have changed so deeply how we design and understand interacting electrons in solids, or produced a programmable platform that so many others have taken up.
